submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 at 3.0 cm thickness achieves the best possible pion/kaon separation performance of 4.6σ at 10 GeV/c, representing a substantial 21% advantage over Radiator-R1 (3.8σ) and 58.6% advantage over Radiator-R3 (2.9σ). 

Comprehensive simulations across the full allowed thickness range (1-6 cm) confirmed that 3.0 cm is the optimal thickness for R2, with fine-grained verification simulations at 2.75 cm (4.563σ) and 3.25 cm (4.493σ) confirming the peak at 3.0 cm.

While Radiator-R1 features hydrophobic treatment for moisture resistance, this advantage is significantly mitigated by the dry nitrogen flush operating environment. Without documented degradation data showing R2 reliability issues, the substantial 0.8σ performance improvement (21% gain) provides meaningfully better hadron identification capability and directly fulfills the primary project goal of achieving the best possible separation.

The recommended configuration meets all constraints: thickness within 1-6 cm range, suitable for long-term operation in the dry nitrogen environment, and represents one of the three approved candidates. R2's 4.6σ separation at 3 cm represents the peak performance across all 20+ simulations conducted.
